bf16.specials: IEEE inf/NaN on exp=255; same range as FP32, less precision

fp8_e4m3fn.specials: OCP: no inf; NaN only S.1111.111; max finite ±448

why_one_value_is_not_enough: The representation error of a single constant (0.1) ranks the formats by significand width, which is true but incomplete. Training precision also depends on exponent range (overflow/underflow of activations and grads), accumulation width (master weights typically remain FP32), rounding mode, hardware throughput (tensor-core generation), and whether a scaling scheme (loss scaling, per-tensor FP8 scaling, MX block scaling) is available. BF16, FP8, and block-scaled FP4 are distinct options with different requirements; they are not drop-in replacements.

recommendation.rationale: Apple MPS is visible to this PyTorch build, but the assignment suite is pinned to CPU in configs/default.yaml for a deterministic, GPU-free grade path. Training precision for the measured runs is therefore FP32. MPS FP16/BF16 was not benchmarked and is not recommended on the basis of the 0.1 encoding error alone. CUDA BF16 mixed precision is the usual large-model default, and it is not available here.

options_considered.fp32: Full exponent range and 23-bit fraction; baseline on CPU; slowest on GPUs that have tensor cores.
options_considered.bf16: Same exponent range as FP32 (bias 127), 7-bit fraction; good default mixed-precision compute dtype on Ampere+ and many TPUs; still uses FP32 accumulation.
options_considered.fp8_e4m3fn: 4-bit exponent, max 448, no infinities; needs scaling (Transformer Engine delayed scaling or MXFP8). Not usable as an unscaled global training dtype.
options_considered.block_scaled_fp4: Element type plus a shared block scale (e.g. MXFP4). Distinct from BF16/FP8; requires supporting hardware and a scale-aware stack. Not recommended here.
